events.title: Virginia Dare Is Born on Roanoke Island
events.description: Virginia Dare was born in the English colony on Roanoke Island, in present-day North Carolina. She was the first child born to English parents in the Americas. Her grandfather, Governor John White, later returned to England for supplies. When he came back, the colony had vanished.
events.significance: Her birth is a landmark of early English settlement in North America. It is also tied to the enduring mystery of the 'Lost Colony.'

events.title: Helium Is Detected During a Solar Eclipse
events.description: French astronomer Pierre Janssen studied the Sun's atmosphere during a total solar eclipse in India. He saw a bright yellow spectral line that did not match any known element. It was later recognized as a new element, helium.
events.significance: Helium was identified in the Sun before it was found on Earth. That made it a milestone for astronomy and spectroscopy.

events.title: Tennessee Delivers the Final Vote for Women's Suffrage
events.description: Tennessee became the 36th state to ratify the 19th Amendment to the U.S. Constitution. The vote in its House of Representatives was famously close. Ratification by three-fourths of the states cleared the amendment's last hurdle.
events.significance: The ratification guaranteed American women the constitutional right to vote. It was a major victory after decades of activism.

events.title: Hardliners Detain Gorbachev, Starting the Soviet Coup Attempt
events.description: A delegation of senior officials visited Soviet President Mikhail Gorbachev at his holiday home at Foros in Crimea. They demanded that he resign or hand over power. He refused, and the group placed him under house arrest, which began a short-lived coup attempt in Moscow.
events.significance: The coup collapsed within days. It sped up the end of Communist Party rule and the breakup of the Soviet Union later that year.
